title: Empire State Manufacturing Survey, October 2026 — the first regional Fed prices-paid read of the month
source: EST: newyorkfed.org/survey/empire/empiresurvey_overview — the New York Fed's own survey overview page, fetched direct 2026-09-08 (HTTP 200) TWICE and independently: first by the cpi-2026-10-14 D-36 pulse-check adjacency sweep that proposed this entry, then re-fetched by this event's own never-assessed initial research the same day. Both reads return the same 2026 release calendar month by month — Jan 15, Feb 17, Mar 16, Apr 15, May 15, Jun 15, Jul 15, Aug 17 as released, then Sep 15, OCT 15, Nov 16, Dec 15 forward — and the same verbatim timing: 'Released at or shortly after 8:30 a.m.' The month-by-month pattern is internally consistent (the 15th, rolled to the next business day when the 15th is a weekend: Feb 15 2026 was a Sunday and the page shows Feb 17; Aug 15 was a Saturday and the page shows Aug 17; Oct 15 2026 is a Thursday, so no roll applies). Filed estimate on two counts, neither of which is doubt about the date: this calendar's confirmed-prefix taxonomy in market-events-data.ts has no slot for a regional Reserve Bank's own survey schedule (there is FED: for the federalreserve.gov FOMC calendar only), and this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep — the same two reasons eurostat-hicp-final-2026-09-17 was filed estimate off its publisher's own primary. Checked 2026-09-08
notes: CANONICAL entry written 2026-09-08 by this event's own never-assessed initial research, which read the one proposal that existed for this id (proposals/empire-state-mfg-2026-10-15.from-cpi-2026-10-14.json, filed by the CPI D-36 sweep) and re-verified its primary independently. The proposal's coverage-gap argument stands: this calendar tracks chicago-pmi and dallas-fed-mfg for other months but carried ZERO regional Federal Reserve manufacturing surveys for October, and Empire State is the first regional Fed survey of each month. Initial research (docs/research/events/empire-state-mfg-2026-10-15.md) then measured two things the proposal could not. FIRST, the release splits into two halves with opposite information content: on FRED's own NY Fed series the headline general-business-conditions index has a lag-1 autocorrelation of 0.269 since 2024 (0.558 since 2021) with a mean absolute month-over-month change of 11.5 points, so an AR(1) two-step forecast of the October headline carries a 90% band of roughly -16 to +32 and cuts uncertainty by only ~5% against the unconditional distribution — the headline is very nearly unforecastable. The prices-paid index autocorrelates at 0.936 over the same window and its two-step band cuts uncertainty ~52%. Read prices, not the headline, and the reason is measured rather than preferred. SECOND, 2026-10-15 is the WORST morning of Empire's visible 2026 schedule for reading it: at 8:30 ET it prints simultaneously with retail sales (high, confirmed CENSUS:), PPI (medium, confirmed BLS:) and — discovered by this research and proposed in the same PR — the Philadelphia Fed's Manufacturing Business Outlook Survey, whose own primary lists 'October 15, 2026 at 8:30 a.m.' Of the four months this calendar has schedules for (Sep 15, Oct 15, Nov 16, Dec 15), October is the only one where Empire shares 8:30 with both BLS and Census majors; on Sep 15 and Nov 16 it prints effectively alone. Any tape move that morning is unattributable to this survey. Impact LOW and symbols empty, deliberately: no house playbook is keyed to regional surveys, none of the nine tracked names carries a New-York-district manufacturing channel, and the headline is a diffusion index over roughly 100 respondents, not a price level, so it can never confirm or refute a CPI print. What the entry buys is that the 10-15 stack is honestly counted and that the Empire/Philly prices-paid pair — which diverged in August 2026 at the 96th percentile of 301 months of disagreement — gets adjudicated on a date the calendar can see. This entry is an ESTIMATE, which widens caution and licenses nothing.
